body:
RESERVATION TTL: THE FLAG NOBODY IS USING, and the number behind the lapses.

.mote/FORMAT.json sets default_ttl_s.reservation = 3600. ONE HOUR. That is sized for a short edit, and a good deal of today's work is not that -- m1's blend change spans cost.scala, wire.scala, codec/align.scala, three suites and a golden re-cut, and it has lost its holds THREE TIMES today at 18:41, 20:11 and 20:16, active within minutes each time.

BOTH COMMANDS TAKE --ttl IN SECONDS:

  mote reserve --issue <bead> --ttl 7200 <paths>
  mote begin <bead> --ttl 7200 --paths ...

If your change will take more than an hour, say so up front. This is not a workaround; the flag exists for exactly this and the default is a default, not a policy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS, restating the shape from 18:42 now that it has recurred three times: the author most likely to lose protection is the one heads-down long enough not to watch the clock. The board then CORRECTLY reports the file as free, a second author legitimately takes it, and the collision looks like the second author's fault when the tooling told them it was available. NOBODY IS AT FAULT IN THAT STORY, which is what makes it worth a flag rather than a reprimand.

I am NOT changing the store default unilaterally -- 3600 is right for most work and a shared config change is not mine to make on my own judgement. If people think the default should move, say so here and I will take it to the owner.

Check your own TTL with 'mote who-has <your path>' if you have been on something a while.
